curricula.title: Kindergarten · Little group
curricula.intro: At this age the goal is joyful exposure: they understand before they speak. Aim for 3–4 words per fortnight, taught with real objects, sounds and movement, and repeat the same song across both weeks.

curricula.title: Kindergarten · Middle group
curricula.intro: Target: by May, each child answers "What's your name?" and "What colour is it?", counts to 5, names about 60 words and sings 8–10 songs.

curricula.title: Kindergarten · Older groups
curricula.intro: Both older groups follow the same plan. Target: by May, each child holds a four-line dialogue (name, age, feelings, likes), counts to 10, names about 120 words and follows simple classroom instructions in English. Week 1 of each theme introduces words, weeks 2–3 add the phrases, week 4 is a game or mini show.

curricula.title: Grade 2 · Spotlight 2
curricula.intro: Grade 2 skips the alphabet and letter pages of Spotlight 2 and starts with the Starter. Each module has a four-week core; where a module spans more weeks, repeat the favourite Lesson B games and add review rounds.

curricula.title: Grade 8 · Spotlight 8
curricula.intro: Modules 1–2 come from the teacher's plan; modules 3–8 follow the Spotlight 8 book (see the Grade 8 check at the top). Grade 8 is a year from the ОГЭ, so each module includes one exam-style speaking slot (interview questions or a 2-minute monologue).

modules.keyLanguage: mummy, daddy, grandma, grandpa, brother, sister, baby · Who's this? It's my sister. · He's tall. She's happy. · Have you got a brother? Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.

modules.title: Module 3: All the things I like!
modules.keyLanguage: jelly, chicken, lemonade, orange juice, milk, water, bread, cheese · sandwich, apple, banana, crisps, biscuits · I like… / He likes… · Does he like…? Yes, he does. · Can I have some…, please? Here you are.

modules.keyLanguage: doll, ball, train, teddy bear, puppet, soldier, jack-in-the-box · this / that / these / those · plurals · It's got a red hat and blue eyes. · I want a…

modules.title: Module 5: Furry friends!

modules.title: Module 6: Home, sweet home!
modules.keyLanguage: living room, bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, garden · sofa, armchair, bed, table, wardrobe, fridge, cooker · Where's Grandma? She's in the kitchen. · There's a… / There are… · in, on, under, next to

modules.title: Module 7: A day off!
modules.keyLanguage: reading, playing, watching TV, swimming, riding a bike, flying a kite · What are you doing? I'm… · What's he doing? He's…

modules.title: Module 8: Day by day
modules.keyLanguage: days of the week · What time is it? It's seven o'clock. · get up, have breakfast, go to school, have lunch, play, go to bed · On Mondays I…

modules.title: Review and show
modules.notes: Weeks 1–2: mega-review games across all modules (Baamboozle, Board race, Hot seat). Weeks 3–4: rehearse and perform two songs and a short dialogue for parents or another class.

modules.title: Starter and Module 1: Family and friends
modules.keyLanguage: family words · tall, short, young, old · long / short / curly hair · She's got long hair. · What's he doing? He's… · My best friend is…

modules.title: Module 2: A working day
modules.keyLanguage: doctor, nurse, vet, pilot, police officer, firefighter, postman, farmer, teacher · hospital, café, baker's, toy shop, sports centre · What does your mum do? She's a vet. She works at… · always, usually, sometimes, never

modules.title: Module 3: Tasty treats
modules.keyLanguage: tomato, egg, flour, sugar, butter, milk, cheese, lemon · some / any · Is there any milk? Yes, there's some. · How much…? How many…? · a lot of

modules.title: Module 4: At the zoo
modules.keyLanguage: giraffe, hippo, monkey, crocodile, elephant, lion, zebra, penguin, dolphin, seal, kangaroo · The monkey is climbing now. Monkeys eat fruit. · bigger, taller, faster · You must… / You mustn't…

modules.title: Module 5: Where were you yesterday?
modules.keyLanguage: was / were · happy, sad, hungry, thirsty, tired, scared · first, second, third… · My birthday is on the fifth of May. · Were you at the park? Yes, I was.

modules.title: Module 6: Tell the tale!
modules.keyLanguage: played, watched, jumped, danced, visited, walked, climbed · Once upon a time… · The hare and the tortoise

modules.title: Module 7: Days to remember
modules.keyLanguage: went, saw, ate, had, made, came, flew, took · Did you…? Yes, I did. / No, I didn't. · the best, the biggest, the funniest

modules.title: Module 8: Places to go
modules.keyLanguage: suitcase, sunhat, camera, swimsuit, sunglasses · beach, mountains, forest, city · I'm going to… · What / Where / When / Who / Why / How…?

modules.title: Review and show
modules.notes: Same shape as grade 3: two weeks of cross-module review games, then two weeks rehearsing a short play or a "Grade 4 news show" for parents.

stages.name: Hello circle
stages.description: Same Hello song every lesson; greet each child by name with a high five

stages.name: Words and actions
stages.description: Teach 3–5 theme words, each with its own gesture; children copy and echo. Then play one quick round: Loud and quiet (say it like a mouse, then a lion), Magic finger (draw the word's picture in the air) or What's missing? with pictures on the board

stages.name: Action song
stages.description: One theme song with gestures, repeated over the whole theme

stages.name: Game
stages.description: One movement or pointing game with the theme words; older groups play two short rounds

stages.name: Make or colour
stages.description: Quick colouring, sticker or craft; name colours and objects while they work

stages.name: Goodbye
stages.description: Same Goodbye song; stamp or sticker for everyone

stages.name: Warm-up routine
stages.description: Hello song or chant, "How are you?" round, weather and date

stages.name: Recall
stages.description: Flashcards of the words from their textbook; Flash and guess, What's missing?

stages.name: Model the chunk
stages.description: You and a volunteer act the target mini-dialogue; class repeats in chorus, then halves, then rows

stages.name: Practice game
stages.description: A controlled speaking game from the Games bank

stages.name: Pair talk
stages.description: Pairs repeat the dialogue with their own words; three pairs perform

stages.name: Goodbye
stages.description: Team points, exit phrase at the door ("Tell me one animal")

stages.name: Warm-up
stages.description: The module song from the Spotlight CD

stages.name: Quick recall
stages.description: Wordwall or Baamboozle round on the projector

stages.name: Big game
stages.description: A freer game: survey, Guess who, Shop role-play

stages.name: Mini performance
stages.description: Groups of 3–4 prepare and show a 30-second scene, chant or show-and-tell

stages.name: Goodbye
stages.description: Team points, sticker chart

stages.name: Hook
stages.description: Picture, video clip, odd question or Would you rather on the module theme

stages.name: Activate language
stages.description: Rapid vocabulary and phrase recall from the module; sentence frames on the board

stages.name: Main speaking task
stages.description: Role-play, survey, debate, interview or game; everyone speaks, you circulate and note errors

stages.name: Report back
stages.description: Pairs or groups share one result; you give three quick recasts from your notes

stages.name: Wrap-up
stages.description: One-line exit ticket: "Today I can…"
